# Moving to ClimateData

[`climakitae`](https://github.com/cal-adapt/climakitae) is moving to one supported
data-access interface: [`ClimateData`](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/api/climate-data/).
The older data-access methods have served us well, but maintaining multiple interfaces
has made it harder to improve the library, document the right patterns, and keep
behavior consistent.

We are beginning the process of retiring the legacy interface (`get_data()`). The goal is to
remove the remaining legacy data-access methods in `2.0.0`, targeted for Q1 or Q2
2027.

## Why make this change?

The newer interface gives us a clearer foundation for future work:

- Queries use catalog-native names and a consistent fluent API.
- Data transformations are explicit processors in the query pipeline.
- Validation and data access are handled in one architecture.
- Documentation and examples can point to one supported way to retrieve data.

This is a maintenance change as much as an API change. We want the development team to
spend their energy on innovative features and improvements, not maintenance.

## What is changing?

The migration work is happening in stages.

Legacy entrypoints such as these are deprecated and will be removed in `2.0.0`:

- [`DataParameters.retrieve()`](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/legacy/data-interface/#climakitae.core.data_interface.DataParameters.retrieve)
- [`get_data_options()`](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/legacy/data-interface/#climakitae.core.data_interface.get_data_options)
- [`get_subsetting_options()`](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/legacy/data-interface/#climakitae.core.data_interface.get_subsetting_options)
- [`get_data()`](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/legacy/data-interface/#climakitae.core.data_interface.get_data)

They now emit `DeprecationWarning` messages that point to the replacement
interface and the removal timeline.

Several older analysis workflows have already been removed because their
functionality is covered by the newer architecture or because they are no
longer maintained:

- The legacy [`WarmingLevels` class](https://github.com/cal-adapt/climakitae/blob/v1.5.9/climakitae/explore/warming.py#L64) 
- The [CmipOpt](https://github.com/cal-adapt/climakitae/blob/v1.5.9/climakitae/explore/uncertainty.py#L18) uncertainty workflow
- The legacy [TimeSeries](https://github.com/cal-adapt/climakitae/blob/v1.5.9/climakitae/explore/timeseries.py#L14) workflow
- The legacy [threshold data-loading wrapper](https://github.com/cal-adapt/climakitae/blob/v1.5.9/climakitae/explore/thresholds.py#L7)

`ClimateData`'s underlying [processors](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/api/processors/) for warming-level and threshold-processing capabilities
remain available. Some shared internal utilities and higher-level workflows
still need follow-up migration work and are not being removed all at once.

## What does this mean for users?

For users who already use [ClimateData](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/api/climate-data/), there is no change. Your existing queries
are where the project is headed, and new features will continue to target that API.

For users who still use the legacy interface, migration is required before the
`2.0.0` release in Q1 or Q2 2027. The main change is replacing the old
GUI-shaped arguments with catalog-native query methods and processors.

### Before

```python
from climakitae.core.data_interface import get_data

data = get_data(
    variable="Air Temperature at 2m",
    resolution="9 km",
    timescale="daily",
    downscaling_method="Dynamical",
    scenario=["Historical Climate", "SSP 3-7.0"],
    area_subset="CA counties",
    cached_area=["Los Angeles County"],
)
```

### After

```python
from climakitae import ClimateData

data = (
    ClimateData()
    .catalog("cadcat")
    .activity_id("WRF")
    .institution_id("UCLA")
    .experiment_id(["historical", "ssp370"])
    .table_id("day")
    .grid_label("d02")
    .variable_id("t2")
    .processes({"clip": "Los Angeles County"})
    .get()
)
```

The migration is more than a spelling change: legacy values such as `"9 km"`
and `"Dynamical"` become catalog values such as `"d02"` and `"WRF"`. The
[Legacy to ClimateData migration guide](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/migration/legacy-to-climate-data/) shows the
full mapping and more examples.

## When should I migrate?

Please migrate legacy data-access code during the `1.x` release line rather
than waiting for `2.0.0`. The target removal date is Q1 or Q2 2027, and warning
messages are intended to give applications, notebooks, and downstream tools
time to move.

A practical migration path is:

1. Replace imports from `climakitae.core.data_interface` with
   `from climakitae import ClimateData`.
2. Replace `.variable(...)` with `.variable_id(...)` if you are using `ClimateData`.
3. Translate legacy resolution, timescale, scenario, and downscaling values to
   `grid_label`, `table_id`, `experiment_id`, and `activity_id`.
4. Replace area-selection arguments with the `clip` processor.
5. Run your existing analysis and compare a small result against the legacy
   workflow before switching production code.

## What stays the same?

The climate data, catalogs, and scientific concepts are not changing. The goal is to 
preserve the results users need while making the route to those results more consistent and maintainable.

Some specialized legacy analysis workflows may need their own migration plan.
We will document those changes separately.

For current query examples, start with the [ClimateData overview](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/climate-data-interface/), our [migration guide](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/migration/legacy-to-climate-data/), or our [example notebooks](https://cal-adapt.github.io/climakitae/dev/notebook-gallery/)
